entrypoint: QueueStore(..., latest_snapshot_reads=True); default False retains strict per-operation history verification.
contract: Opt-in constructor performs existing locked strict history verification before returning.

Every operational read uses the actual final complete WAL record bytes, verifies checksum/snapshot envelope/positive sequence, and reads fresh current state under the existing stable-inode exclusive flock.
No stat memo and no checkpoint/cache-supplied state. Tail scan scales with final record size, not total history.
Each instance tracks a sequence floor from startup, successful reads, and validated durable own commits. Observed sequence rollback, missing WAL, and empty WAL after state exists are refused.

Historical corruption and historical sequence-chain faults that leave the latest complete record valid are deliberately detected at strict startup or explicit audit(), rather than every operational read.
Explicit audit() always uses existing strict history verification and refuses rollback below this instance sequence floor.
Cooperating cross-process writers retain the existing exclusive lock through read/change/append; claims therefore use latest current active ownership state.
No compaction, WAL format change, or bulk WAL rewrite. Existing torn-final evidence preservation/truncation is retained inside operational recovery; actual live WAL was never opened by this audit.
limitations: This intentionally changes the historical-integrity failure contract and requires explicit review before any GPU worker activation.
No durable antirollback anchor is added: a valid truncated prefix presented to a fresh process can pass strict startup, as in the original store. A running instance detects sequence regression.
A same-sequence replacement containing a new valid self-checksummed snapshot is outside existing accidental-corruption checksum guarantees; no malicious owner/root security claims.

Noncooperating in-place writes can race filesystem reads as before; metadata comparison detects common races but is not claimed to authenticate bytes. Unlike rejected stat memo, every operational read rechecks actual record bytes.
Per-read time scales with final record and JSON snapshot size; synthetic benchmark uses large audit data with an empty jobs map.
Benchmark startup strict replay ran first and built replay sidecar; subsequent baseline_cold timing is a cached-prefix strict read, not raw replay.
